_meta.conventions: null = not found/unverified. 'verification' fields say how solid each item is. Aggregator-only facts are flagged.

open_eds_accepting_911.name: Mission Hospital (main campus, incl. Mission Children's Hospital)
open_eds_accepting_911.operator: Mission Health / HCA Healthcare (MH Mission Hospital, LLLP)
open_eds_accepting_911.trauma_level: ACS-verified Level I trauma center (verification announced Dec 3, 2025; ACS survey Sept 2025; 3-year term). Previously Level II since the program began in 1995. Only Level I in WNC, 7th in NC. NC OEMS state designation record not separately checked.
open_eds_accepting_911.notes: Adult ER plus a dedicated pediatric ER (North Tower); Mission Children's Hospital is on the 3rd floor of the main building. ER entrance = Entrance 1 at the main hospital, 24/7. Air medical: Mountain Area Medical Airlift (MAMA). Context: hospital has had repeated CMS 'immediate jeopardy' findings (BPR, Dec 2025). Correction to the brief: Mission is no longer Level II.

open_eds_accepting_911.name: Mission Hospital - St. Joseph campus
open_eds_accepting_911.status_2026: open as a hospital campus (part of Mission Hospital)
open_eds_accepting_911.notes: Mission's official materials list the adult and pediatric ERs only at the main hospital (509 Biltmore Ave); the Mission locations page lists 'South Asheville ER' as the only other ER. One aggregator (Vivian Health) claims an ED here; treat it as unreliable. Do not route 911 ambulances here unless confirmed locally.

open_eds_accepting_911.name: South Asheville ER (Mission Hospital freestanding ED)
open_eds_accepting_911.operator: Mission Health / HCA Healthcare (licensed as part of Mission Hospital)
open_eds_accepting_911.address: 2512 Hendersonville Rd, Arden, NC 28704 (corner of Airport Rd and Hendersonville Rd)

hospitals_ed.other_notes: I found no other ED inside Buncombe County. Urgent-care clinics (e.g., Mission My Care Now, AdventHealth/Pardee urgent cares) are not EDs and were not inventoried. Nearest EDs just outside the county (AdventHealth Hendersonville, Pardee/UNC Health in Henderson County, Haywood Regional, etc.) were not researched.

system_notes: Buncombe 911 center describes itself as serving 8 law enforcement agencies and 21 fire departments (buncombenc.gov 911 page, seen only in search results; the site blocks automated fetches). The list above has 19 departments plus airport ARFF.

In April 2026 county commissioners voted to merge 20 fire protection/ambulance-rescue tax districts into one unified fire district. Biltmore Forest, Asheville, Weaverville and Black Mountain keep paying through municipal taxes. Departments appear to remain separate operators. Source: buncombenc.gov via search results plus the Citizen-Times headline (AOL syndication); article body not readable.
Montreat is served by Black Mountain FD. Biltmore Forest is served by Skyland FD Station 4. The North Buncombe district is served by Weaverville FD.

ems_stations.provider: Buncombe County EMS (county-run; part of Buncombe County Emergency Services)
ems_stations.co_location_with_fire: YES. The 2023 consultant study says 'EMS is principally a guest within existing fire stations'. County officials said the same in March 2026, and WLOS (Sept 2025) adds that ambulances also park at hospitals. EMS East (Swannanoa, about Feb–Mar 2027) will be the county's first standalone EMS station.

fleet_and_staffing.bases_2024: 10 EMS bases, 'from Weaverville to Arden, Candler to Black Mountain' (Mountain Xpress, June 13, 2024). The 2022 study recommended 12 more.
fleet_and_staffing.ambulances: 2022/23 study: 12 24-hour ambulances plus 1 peak-demand unit; 13 needed for daytime peak and 19 total recommended. Mid-2024: 14–15 ambulances at daytime peak, 4–5 spares, 97 paramedics, about 30 on duty at peak.

response_time_goals_and_performance.stated_goal: 8 minutes 59 seconds or less, 90% of the time (called the industry standard in the 2023 study; EMS Division Manager Jamison Judd restated it as the goal in Nov 2025).
response_time_goals_and_performance.tiered_model_recommended_2022_study: Urban: 8-minute travel time at 90%. Suburban: 10-minute travel at 80%. Rural: 12-minute travel at 70%.
response_time_goals_and_performance.actual: 2016–2022: from 911 call to EMS arrival was 17 min 17 s at the 90th percentile; EMS response (dispatch to arrival) missed the 8:59 target by 6 min 3 s. 2021–22 90th percentile was over 16 min. Average response about 15.5 min (Spectrum News, Nov 2025). The 2018 analysis found 76% of critical calls answered in under 8 min, using different methods.
response_time_goals_and_performance.workload: 184,964 EMS records over 6 years (about 31k/yr). 60% of incidents result in transport. Peak calls 11am–5pm, staying high until 10pm+. Fire first responders reach about 77% of non-Alpha medical calls and arrive before EMS on 68.7% of those. Calls up about 20% since 2020; +6,681 calls from FY21 to FY22.

venues.name: HomeTrust Park (formerly McCormick Field) - Asheville Tourists
venues.capacity: 4,000 seats (renovation architect EwingCole; Wikipedia lists the same, uncited)
venues.affiliation: High-A affiliate of the Houston Astros (South Atlantic League)
venues.typical_event_times: 2026 pattern (July series vs Winston-Salem): Wed–Fri 6:35 pm, Sat 6:05 pm, Sun 1:05 pm. BPR also notes a 6:35 pm standard. Times vary by series; season runs about April–September (2026 home opener Apr 21).
venues.attendance: 2025: 163,380 total, 2,553 average per game, 8th in the South Atlantic League. 2024: 183,987 total (about 2,831/game). Source is an aggregator (The Baseball Cube). Both seasons were played during the renovation.
venues.parking: Very limited on-site parking. About 50 pass-holder spaces at Memorial Stadium lot above the park. Main option is Ironwood Parking Garage (45 Federal Alley, behind Swannanoa Cleaners on Coxe Ave), 0.4 mi away, $2/hr, with a free Gray Line trolley shuttle from 60 min before first pitch until the game ends.
venues.notes: Renamed HomeTrust Park Apr 14, 2026 after an 18-month, ~$40M renovation (Aug 2024–Apr 2026). The 2026 opener was a sellout. The lease requires 35,000 non-baseball attendees per year.

venues.name: The Orange Peel
venues.capacity: 1,050 standing, general admission (venue tech page). Wikipedia says a 2009 expansion brought it to 1,100.
venues.typical_event_times: Most shows: doors 7 pm, show 8 pm; some doors 6 pm, show 7 pm (October 2026 calendar). Box office opens 4 pm on show days.

venues.name: Hellbender by the Orange Peel (NEW outdoor amphitheater)

venues.coord_source: APPROXIMATE (no county point for 151; placed just east of the 131 Thompson St point)
venues.typical_event_times: Limited 2026 season (first concert Aug 1, 2026) running to October; full season from spring 2027. Shows must end by 10 pm. Example: Oct 14, 2026 show had doors 4:30 pm, show 6 pm.
venues.parking: Shuttles from Asheville Mall (lower level of the former JCPenney), about 10 minutes each way. Private lots nearby $15–30. In July 2026, pedestrians walking Swannanoa River Rd after dark needed APD and traffic-control help.
venues.notes: On the former Cursus Keme brewery site, which closed after Helene. This is a new 6,000-person event generator near Biltmore Village and the Swannanoa River Rd / I-240 / Tunnel Rd corridor; worth modeling.

venues.name: Biltmore Estate
venues.address: Entrance: 1 Lodge St, Asheville, NC 28803 (Lodge Gate, Biltmore Village)
venues.capacity: 8,000-acre estate. Main lots near the house: A and B (8–10 min walk), C (RV), E (park-and-ride with shuttle). No published vehicle capacity found.
venues.typical_event_times: Daytime admission plus Candlelight Christmas Evenings, Nov 3, 2026–Jan 9, 2027 (Biltmore tickets page; some secondary sources say through Jan 10). Evening entry times not listed on the tickets page.
venues.attendance: About 1.4 million visitors (FY2023 economic impact study via Asheville Watchdog). About 85% from outside Buncombe; $250.3M spent off-estate. Candlelight visitor counts: NOT FOUND.
venues.entry_exit_routing: Entry (official): I-40 Exit 50/50B to US-25 (Hendersonville Rd) north, then the far-left lane onto All Souls Crescent to the Lodge Gate at 1 Lodge St. It is 3 miles from the gate/reception to Biltmore House. Exit: NOT found in Biltmore's official materials. OpenStreetMap shows the one-way inbound Approach Road and the outbound 'Biltmore Estate Drive' (partly one-way) both meeting public streets at Biltmore Village (Lodge St/US-25A and McDowell St/All Souls Crescent/US-25). I found no verified public exit gate straight onto Hendersonville Rd south of the village, so do not assume one without confirmation. Biltmore's directions say visitors pass the Gardens, Conservatory, Farm, Antler Hill Village and Winery on the way to the exit.

venues.access: Off NC-191 (Brevard Rd) at Blue Ridge Parkway MP 393.6. I-26's new Exit 35 to Frederick Law Olmsted Way is due by end of 2026.

lodging_supply.note: From Explore Asheville CEO Vic Isley's Feb 2026 board presentation, as reported by Mountain Xpress. I read it only in search excerpts (the article returned 403). An older count was 'nearly 8,000 rooms' (Mountain Xpress, undated).

peak_months.summary: October (leaf season) is the peak month. STR data has shown October as the top hotel-revenue month for several years (about $50M in one older report, with a record 86.2% occupancy in that older period; exact year not confirmed). Peak-day visitor counts: NOT FOUND in any source.
peak_months.derived_only: Simple average: 13.9M visitors / 365 = about 38,000 visitor arrivals per day in 2023. This is my arithmetic, not a sourced peak-day figure, and it is not a count of people present.

leaf_peak_timing.summary: Asheville (about 2,100 ft) usually peaks in the third to fourth week of October, running into the first days of November. Higher elevations (Craggy, Mt. Mitchell) peak early-to-mid October, and color moves downhill about 1,000 ft every 7–10 days. Sources are travel/lodging guides, not an agency forecast.

helene_effects.summary: Q4 2024 was projected at about a 70% revenue loss (about $585M) for tourism and hospitality. 10,000–12,000 service workers applied for disaster unemployment. Hotels had their best-ever January occupancy in 2025 because of recovery workers. Summer 2025 was uneven: some B&Bs were at about 15% occupancy versus 90% before the storm, while Pisgah Inn was 85% booked for October. Spending kept falling in 2025 (−2.1%) even as some mountain regions grew. Blue Ridge Parkway reopenings continued into 2026, and I-40 through the Pigeon River Gorge is still down to one lane each way.

aadt_data_service.notes: Stations layer: 878 Buncombe points with LocationID, Located_On, Approach, Crossroad, Latitude, Longitude and AADT_2002..AADT_2025. Query with where=County='Buncombe'. Most surface-street stations are counted in even years (latest 2024); most mainline interstate stations have no count after 2023. The segments layer has 2025 AADT for every segment plus K_FACTOR, D_FACTOR and truck percentages. Data last edited about Sept 2026. Map page: https://connect.ncdot.gov/resources/State-Mapping/pages/traffic-volume-maps.aspx

projects_2026.name: I-26 Connector (Asheville)
projects_2026.status: Groundbreaking Apr 23, 2026. About $1.8B, design-build (Archer-Wright JV). Completion late 2031 (NCDOT page: Oct 2031). Year-one traffic impacts expected to be minimal apart from ramps already closed near the Jeff Bowen Bridge. Section C (I-40 interchanges with Smokey Park Hwy, I-26/I-240 and Brevard Rd) was being reprioritized for funding, schedule not final. Will separate interstate from local traffic on the Patton Ave / Bowen Bridge corridor and build a new French Broad crossing north to US 19/23/70.

projects_2026.name: I-26 widening, Asheville (I-40) to Hendersonville
projects_2026.status: July 17, 2026: all 4 westbound lanes open in final configuration from US 64 (Exit 49) to Brevard Rd (Exit 33). A short eastbound section is still 2 lanes. About 6 months of work remain west of the Blue Ridge Parkway bridge, with overnight closures for diamond grinding and markings. New Exit 35 (to Frederick Law Olmsted Way, built for the Pratt & Whitney plant) is due by end of 2026. Buncombe section completion: 'expected January 2027' (Jan 2026 report); NCDOT's June 2025 contract date was July 1, 2027. The Henderson County section is functionally complete.

projects_2026.name: Helene road closures (2026)
projects_2026.status: NCDOT (July 31, 2026): more than 99% of Helene-damaged roads have reopened. I found no specific Buncombe road still closed. The big remaining closures are outside the county but shape regional routing: (1) I-40 Pigeon River Gorge (Haywood County, toward Tennessee) runs one lane each way; $2.8B rebuild, target 2 EB + 1 WB lanes by late 2028 and completion late 2029; a 35 mph limit was reported. (2) Hickory Nut Gorge, US 64/US 74A toward Chimney Rock/Lake Lure, permanent repairs to 2029. (3) US 176 Saluda–Tryon closed until late 2029. All Blue Ridge Parkway sections in Buncombe were open as of Oct 6, 2026.
